summary: Chaotic client-side retry loop causing API gateway 5xx surge and upstream runtime eviction cycle
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC we observed sustained elevated 5xx from the API gateway fronting dedicated tenant FableAI (us-east). Traffic patterns show many short-lived requests followed by aggressive client retries from a single tenant key. The gateway returned a mixture of 502/503/504 and several upstream runtime processes were observed to enter eviction/restart cycles, exacerbating the error rate.

Impact: Customer reports production customer-facing errors; embedding and chat endpoints returning 5xx for ~10% of requests during the peak window. FableAI business impact: degraded user sessions, automated job failures, and support escalations.

Environment: prod; dedicated capacity region us-east; tenant pinned to gpt-medium-v1 variant; Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs.

Observed behavior: Rapid retry loops from client (~50 retries within 30s per failed request), amplified by hedged retry policy at the gateway. Many retries created head-of-line congestion in accept queues and saturated ephemeral connection slots. Upstream serving-runtime processes hit resource pressure (fd exhaustion and elevated CPU threads) and triggered graceful eviction followed by prewarm which increased latency/first-byte-timeouts and more retries.

Expected behavior: Gateway should apply per-tenant retry damping, hedged retries should back off under sustained failures, and serving-runtime should avoid eviction cascade under bursty retransmits.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate high volume of small requests (payloads <1KB) at sustained 200 RPS from a single API key with deterministic client-side retry policy (exponential backoff with short max delay). 2) Configure gateway hedged retry enabled. 3) Observe accept queue growth, 5xx rate at apigw, and runtime worker evictions.

Logs / metrics: 
- apigw logs: repeated 429/502/503 for tenant fableai-tenant-01 with client-id X-Api-Key: fa-prod-01; timestamps 2026-03-10T02:17:xxZ to 02:45:xxZ.
- runtime logs: repeated SIGTERM to worker PID 1123 -> restart -> prewarm -> SIGTERM; nvml/gpu logs show high context-switches and elevated memory fragmentation.
- Observability graphs: accept-queue-depth for us-east apigw surged from 30 -> 420; ephemeral-fd-usage trending to 98% on proxies. Latency P95 rose from 120ms -> 2.4s.

Customer report: FableAI support engineer supplied a client-side timeout/retry config that matches the pattern (max_retries=10, initial_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=500ms). They reported sudden degradation at 02:15 UTC coincident with a release on their side (no certificate changes).

investigation_notes: Accept-queue and ephemeral fd metrics are the strongest signal: when accept-queue > 250 the gateway begins returning 502/504 at a high rate.
Client behavior: deterministic retry pattern without jitter leads to synchronized retransmits amplifying short-lived failures.
Hedged retries at apigw multiply concurrent upstream work — combined with client retries this created >3x the usual inflight requests per connection slot for tenant.
Runtime responded to backlog by sequentially terminating idle workers to reclaim memory; however termination timing overlapped with prewarm causing transient capacity loss.
We reproduced locally with a traffic generator: enabling hedged-retry + aggressive client retries triggers accept-queue climb and repeated runtime SIGTERM within 5-7 minutes.
No evidence of GPU driver crash or hardware fault; resource pressure pattern points to connection storm and scheduling pressure.
Related historical incidents: SUP-421420 (apigw conn thrash during mixed embed/chat burst) shows similar accept-queue thresholds — consider reuse of that runbook.
Telemetry: adding tenant-scoped connection counters and per-route retry amplifiers would help auto-detect and throttle harmful patterns earlier.
mitigation_and_workarounds: Applied tenant-level RPS cap (temporary) to break retry loop
Disabled hedged retries on the route for the tenant to avoid duplicate upstream load
Suggested customer increase client backoff and add jitter (we provided recommended config: initial_backoff=250ms, max_backoff=5000ms, jitter=full)
Worked with customer to deploy a quick client-side patch; observed error rate reduction within 15 minutes of patch rollout
root_cause_hypothesis: Primary: Synchronized client retries combined with gateway hedged-retry produced a thundering herd that saturated accept queues and ephemeral connection slots, leading to upstream timeouts and runtime eviction cycles.

Contributing: Hedged retry defaults are aggressive for high-concurrency small-payload patterns; serving-runtime eviction policy is sensitive to short bursts of connection churn and may benefit from longer grace before termination.
actions_required: Short term: update gateway route config to apply automatic per-tenant retry damping when accept-queue exceeds threshold (owner: apigw team).
Short term: add observability alert for tenant-level retry amplification ratio > 2.5 (owner: observability).
Medium term: runtime team to adjust eviction grace period and prewarm logic to avoid capacity loss during churn (owner: runtime).
Medium term: recommend change to hedged-retry default to include adaptive backoff under sustained errors (owner: apigw).
Follow-up: schedule postmortem with SRE, runtime, and apigw on 2026-03-17 to finalize remediation and rollout plan (owner: Incident Commander).
resolution: Temporary measures applied 2026-03-10: tenant rate-limit and hedged-retry toggle reduced error rate to baseline.
Customer implemented client-side backoff/jitter and confirmed reduction in failures by 2026-03-10 03:35Z.
Incident remains open while medium-term runtime and gateway changes are planned and assigned.
Postmortem scheduled and owners assigned for concrete remediations.
